This storm produced nickel size hail as well as damaging winds.
episodes.212557: On the 6th afternoon to early evening, a moist column combined with dynamic lift from an approaching cool front to produce numerous to widespread training thunderstorms over northern portions of central Indiana.  While most cells were generally sub-severe, isolated damaging winds were most organized in Warren County and most intense at the Muncie airport.  More noteworthy was the quasi-parallel nature of the approaching boundary to the moist conveyor's axis, which produced multiple roudns of heavy rain over several zones, and considerable flash flooding in portions of Warren County and Fountain County where up to an estimated 7.00 inches of rain fell. This severe weather event would be the first of many for the month which would eventually define a formal disaster period from June 6th to the 18th which was declared by the governor of Indiana.
episodes.212567: A cold front swung through the area in the evening kicking off mostly sub severe storms, though a few did produce damaging winds in MA and CT.
episodes.212738: Ahead of an approaching cold front and aided by leading shortwave-induced ascent, a cluster of thunderstorms tracked across southeastern Ohio and western Pennsylvania producing wind damage, several tornadoes, and a few instances of large hail. Moist southerly flow pulled upper 50s to low 60s dew points with surface temperatures in the mid 70s allowing for sufficient destabilization up to 1500 J/kg of MLCAPE, 35-40 knots of effective shear, and 50-150 m2/s2 of 0-1 km SRH to support an all hazards threat.

episodes.213192: Following two rounds of showers and thunderstorms in the morning, a third round later in the day produced damaging wind gusts over northwest Ohio.
episodes.213271: A slow-moving upper low and increasing moisture content contributed to a period of active weather during the weekend of June 5, with scattered showers and thunderstorms occurring across the area mainly in the evening and overnight hours. Flash flooding was the primary weather hazard throughout the weekend, along with isolated instances of hail and damaging winds.
episodes.213691: A passing cold front kicked off isolated severe storms in Central New York. These storms had damaging wind gusts and large hail. A tree fell on two people standing outside of their tent in a campground; both people were injured.
episodes.213744: Showers and thunderstorms affected the combined Panhandles each afternoon and evening in the early parts of June. With enough moisture, instability and sources to provide atmospheric lift, these storms were able to become severe each day and bring large hail to the region. A few instances of damaging winds and flooding also occurred.
episodes.213893: Showers and thunderstorms began to develop during the early afternoon hours across northwestern Pennsylvania with the passage of a potent shortwave diving southeastward out of the Great Lake region on June 6, 2026. Storms gradually trended upscale with some strong-to-severe thunderstorms beginning to form by the afternoon hours within an environment with ample instability (2000 J/kg of CAPE) and bulk shear (30 knots) in place across northwestern Pennsylvania. Wind damage was observed in portions of Warren County during the early afternoon hours before storms across northern Pennsylvania began to weaken. Additional development to the south continued to exhibit upscale growth with more favorable shear and instability in place given less cloud cover, with two broken lines of thunderstorms gradually congealing into one solid line across eastern Pennsylvania. These lines of thunderstorms produced widespread tree damage between the Interstate 80 and 78 corridors. Further south, a bowing segment across southwestern Pennsylvania continued into Somerset County producing destructive wind damage near Somerset. This bow exhibited some weakening as it progressed further east, but continued to produce considerable tree damage across portions of Bedford and Fulton Counties before weakening further.
episodes.213976: A couple rounds of showers and thunderstorms developed across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the morning and afternoon of the 6th, as an upper level disturbance approached the region. Locally heavy rainfall from this activity resulted in some flash flooding in Creek, Tulsa, and Okmulgee Counties.
episodes.214109: During the afternoon and evening of June 5, 2026, a stalled frontal boundary draped from southeast Nebraska into southwest Iowa served as the focal point for thunderstorm development. As an approaching shortwave disturbance provided forcing for ascent, storms initiated along the boundary. The surrounding environment was characterized by strong deep-layer shear and robust instability, capable of supporting all severe hazards. High atmospheric moisture content situated over saturated soils also created efficient rainfall processes, elevating flash flooding concerns. These storms initially erupted as brief, discrete cells before rapidly undergoing upscale growth into a larger convective complex as they moved into southwest Iowa.||As the severe complex traversed southwest Iowa, it produced several areas of severe weather. Isolated large hail up to quarter-size (1.00 inch) was reported. However, as the storms merged and grew upscale, straight-line winds quickly became the dominant threat. Multiple stations measured severe wind gusts peaking at 69 mph, which resulted in significant and widespread tree damage. Notable impacts included uprooted trees in Elliott, a mature walnut tree completely uprooted near Macedonia, and numerous large tree limbs snapped in Carson and Essex before the complex eventually tracked east and weakened.
episodes.214110: During the afternoon and evening of June 5, 2026, a stalled frontal boundary draped from southeast Nebraska into southwest Iowa served as the focal point for severe thunderstorm development. As an approaching shortwave disturbance provided the necessary forcing for ascent, thunderstorms initiated along the boundary. The surrounding environment was characterized by strong deep-layer shear and robust instability, capable of supporting all severe hazards. Additionally, high atmospheric moisture content situated over already saturated soils generated efficient rainfall processes, elevating flash flooding concerns. These storms initially erupted as brief, discrete cells before rapidly undergoing upscale growth into a larger convective complex.||During the initial discrete phase, the dominant hazard was large hail, with hailstones measured up to 2.00 inches in diameter. The rotating updrafts also produced a couple of funnel clouds, including a photographed rope funnel near Hallam and another near Swanton, though they remained aloft, and no tornadoes were confirmed. As the storms merged into a larger complex, the primary threat shifted to damaging straight-line winds. Multiple stations measured severe wind gusts peaking at 68 mph, which resulted in localized thunderstorm wind damage across the region before the system eventually weakened.
episodes.214319: An MCS moved southeastward across Central Ohio in the late morning into the early afternoon on June 6, 2026 moving along the northern edge of a surface high pressure situated in the southeastern United States. Ahead of the MCS, strong warm air advection allowed dew points to rise up into the mid 60s with surface based CAPE of around 1000 J/kg and effective bulk shear of 30 knots creating a severe wind threat. ||Later in the evening on June 6, 2026, a cold front moved south from Michigan and southern Ontario into an environment of around 1500 J/kg of ML CAPE and effective bulk shear of around 40 knots. This created a severe wind threat along the western shores of Lake Erie in Ohio.
episodes.214344: Daytime-to-evening thunderstorm activity occurred on the north/east periphery of a persistent closed low across Texas on the 6th. Several more damaging downburst wind events occurred, including near Ada, OK. Slow-moving thunderstorms also produced reports of flooding in west-central Oklahoma during the evening hours.
episodes.214430: On the evening of June 6, 2026, a cold front moved south from Michigan and southern Ontario into an environment of around 1500 J/kg of ML CAPE and effective bulk shear of around 40 knots. This produce gale to storm force wind gusts over the western portion of Lake Erie and the shoreline.
episodes.214439: During the day on June 6, 2026, a shortwave moved across Lake Erie into Northwestern Pennsylvania. The region had ample warm air advection through the majority of the morning as temperatures and dew points reached into the upper 70s and mid 60s, respectively. ML CAPE rose to around 1000 J/kg and with effective shear of around 30 knots allowed for thunderstorms to generate severe wind gusts.
episodes.214511: A weak upper level system combined with a stalled frontal boundary extending over portions of southeast Louisiana and coastal Mississippi to produce a period of training thunderstorms over parts of Harrison, Hancock, and Pearl River Counties in coastal Mississippi.  Very high moisture content in the atmosphere and warm air in the mid and upper levels allowed for very high rainfall rates to accompany these training thunderstorms resulting in flash flooding.
episodes.214512: A weak upper level system combined with a stalled frontal boundary extending over portions of southeast Louisiana and coastal Mississippi to produce a period of training thunderstorms over parts of southeast Louisiana. episodes.214681: The combination of a stalled frontal boundary and building heat and humidity resulted in an unsettled weather pattern across the Ohio Valley for the start of June. Each day yielded developing showers and thunderstorms across the Midwest and travelling eastward along the front before dissipating after sunset. On June 6th, storms remained strong to severe as it dashed across Ohio, and caused scattered tree and power line damage across Perry County from the damaging wind gusts.
episodes.214870: Scattered showers and thunderstorms pushed across eastern New York during the afternoon hours on June 6, 2026 within the warm sector of a low pressure system. The strongest and most organized thunderstorms moved across Ulster and Dutchess Counties where numerous reports of downed trees and wires occurred. More isolated thunderstorms also produced some downed trees across far northern Washington County and near North Creek.

episodes.214939: During the evening hours on June 5th, storms move into portions of Buffalo and Trempealeau counties producing large hail and strong winds. Eventually, these storms formed into a line and pushed southeast into portions of La Crosse, Monroe and Juneau Counties bring additional large hail, damaging wind gusts and an EF-0 tornado in eastern Monroe County prior to storms exiting to the southeast.
